newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Dec 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Advance Bank shareholders yesterday overwhelmingly approved the A$2.65 billion takeover of their bank by St George and despite earlier contradictory responses, the Australian Securities Commission said it would not oppose the scheme of arrangement for the merger at a scheduled Supreme Court hearing on January 6. Page 1.

High-ranking Malaysian politician Tan Sri Dato Muhammad Bi Muhammad Taib appeared before a Brisbane Magistrates Court yesterday after he was allegedly detected at Brisbane airport with a large mixture of undeclared currency in his possession. The Chief Minister of Selangor State and one of the highest-ranking members of the ruling UMNO party was charged for failing to complete a report under section 15 of the Financial Transactions Reports Act. Page 1.

Under a Federal Government information paper outlining changes to the taxation of foreign-sourced income, the controlled foreign company (CFC) measures would be tightened so that only income earned in a much shortened list of "truly comparable tax countries" would be exempted. Page 3.

Following the release of an independent expert's report that valued Highlands Gold Ltd's shares at well over Placer Dome Inc's takeover offer, Placer said yesterday it was unable to justify any increase in its offer, instead offering to pay A$276.8 million for Highlands' 25 per cent share of the Porgera mine in Papua New Guinea and a further A$20.9 million owed to Highlands by the PNG Government. Page 15.

In a move designed to strengthen its records management division, Brambles Industries Ltd has announced a A$111 million takeover bid for computer and office services company Ausdoc Group Ltd. The Brambles bid is 13 times Ausdoc's 1995-96 earnings before tax and interest and a 23 per cent premium to its A$1.63 closing price yesterday. Page 15.

The AMP Society has continued its push into Latin America's emerging markets by launching a 25 cents a share takeover offer for Perth-based miner Equatorial Mining NL. The bid values Equatorial at just over A$79 million and offers a 3.5 cents premium on yesterday's closing price on the shares AMP does not already own. Page 16.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Advance Bank Australia Ltd shareholders have voted in favour of an agreed cash and scrip takeover by St George Bank Ltd. The result is a boost to the planned A$2.65 billion merger, but the scheme of arrangement still requires Supreme Court approval and shareholders need to approve changes to Advance's articles of association. Page 19.

Coles Myer Ltd has ended its two-year property assets disposal program with the sale of its interest in 12 major retail outlets, including six of its World 4 Kids stores. The A$558 million reaped from the sale will be used to reduce debt in the company to within its target range of 55 to 60 per cent, according to Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels. Page 19.

Claiming that the valuation of Highlands Gold Ltd by independent experts Baring Brother Burrows was "surprisingly high", North American gold giant Placer Dome Inc has offered to cancel its stake in Highlands for A$297 million in return for a 25 per cent interest in the one million-ounce-a-year Porgera gold mine. Page 19.

Adelaide Brighton Cement Ltd is expected to book a profit of up to A$6 million on the A$60 million sale of its New Zealand pipe business, Humes Industries Ltd, to Fletcher Challenge's building products division, while Boral Ltd will realise A$40 million trough the sale of its roof-tile plants at Langenzenn and Riesa-Forberge in Germany. Page 20.

Transport giant Brambles Industries Ltd last night announced a A$111 million all-cash bid for document-exchange company Ausdoc Group Ltd, in an offer that is 40 per cent more than Ausdoc's weighted average share price over the past six months. The offer is subject to at least 90 per cent acceptance from holders of Ausdoc's ordinary shares before Brambles moves to compulsory acquisition. Page 20.

Although ratings agency Standard & Poor's yesterday downgraded The News Corporation Ltd's credit outlook from stable to negative, the agency maintained its investment-grade ratings on more than US$9 billion of the media giant's debt and preference stock isues at either BBB or BBB-. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After Advance Bank shareholders yesterday approved St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover and the Australian Securities Commission dropped direct action against the deal, the chances of success for the merger improved dramatically, but National Australia Bank could still spoil the deal if it decides to launch its own legal action. Page 21.

After deciding to break up its property portfolio rather than pursuing a large float or a partial float, Coles Myer announced yesterday it had sold A$558 million worth of property. The sales include the Chermside centre in Brisbane, Innaloo in Perth and Roselands in Sydney. Page 21.

Announcing Brambles Industries' A$111 million cash takeover bid for document and management services business Ausdoc Group yesterday, Brambles chief executive John Fletcher said the company considers the offer to be attractive for Ausdoc shareholders and xpects Ausdoc directors to support the move. Page 21.

In its second share placement in less than 12 months, casino group Crown raised A$81.9 million yesterday through a placement to institutional investors. Crown placed 32.75 million shares, or 6.17 per cent of the issued capital, at A$2.50 each with investrs. Page 21.

In an effort to strengthen its balance sheet through a reduction of its debt levels, FAI Insurance has raised A$50 million through a preference share issue. FAI chief executive Rodney Adler said yesterday that the injection of County NatWest funds would add significantly to FAI's standing in the financial community. Page 21.

After failing to turn the business around, energy and building products group Boral has sold its German roof-tile operations to Koramic-Weinerberger Dachprodukte GmbH for A$40 million. Yesterday's sale leaves Boral with four brick and two paver plants inthe Netherlands, six brick plants in Germany, one brick plant in Poland and some minor quarrying and resource assets in Europe. Page 23.
THE AGE

St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank was approved by 89.75 per cent of shares represented at yesterday's meeting and Advance chairman Jim Service told the bank's shareholders that the Australian Securities Commission would not be objecting to the merger, despite its announcement last week that it would oppose the deemed proxy provisions in the scheme. Page C1.

Coles Myer has now divested A$830 million in property since July, after announcing yesterday the sale of sites worth A$558 million. The sales included a 50 per cent stake in Ringwood's Eastland shopping complex to its joint-venture partner, Queensland Investment Corporation, as well as the women's fashion shop Katies in Bourke Street. Page C1.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission began proceedings against supermarket chain Safeway in the Federal Court yesterday, alleging that the Victorian division of Woolworths used its market dominance to force Tip Top Bakeries to fix prices. If found guilty of breaching the Trade Practices Act, Safeway could face a fine of up to A$10 million. Page C1.

After international ratings agency Moody's upgraded Victoria from Aa2 to Aa1 yesterday, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said households and businesses would receive a one-off reward if the State achieved its triple -A credit rating by 1999, although he woud not disclose what the reward might be. Page C1.

Victoria has slipped below the growth level of other States for the second quarter in a row, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics' experimental estimate of output in Victoria for September. Victoria's growth increased by 0.2 in September, belw the national average of 0.5 per cent on trend terms. Page C1.

As it announced details of a A$82 million capital raising yesterday, Melbourne casino operator Crown said it expected first-half results to be up on last year, with its first five months of trading to the end of November comparing favourably with the previous corresponding period. Page C3.
